messages:
anya-support: customer escalated — mobile app stream stops mid-response when switching from office WiFi -> cellular (EU region). No client error, UI shows 'stream ended'. request_id=req_0a1b2c. SDK=mobile-js@2.3.1. ticket#12345

support-bot: created ticket 12345 and linked to #support (escalation). :rotating_light:

sam-eng: thanks anya. short question: can you paste the minimal curl repro they used and whatever client logs they have? any proxy/VPN on their carrier?

anya-support: repro they provided — works if you stay on WiFi but if you toggle cellular after ~10-15s, the SSE stops and client never sees an error. they captured the client network log: 

--- client command ---
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-small&prompt=hello"

they also sent a snippet of the browser/mobile console: 
```
SSE: open -> events started
SSE: received chunk 1 {"partial":true}
Network: switch to cellular
(no further SSE events)
(no socket close/error logged)
```

kai-sdks: interesting — client saw chunked data but no FIN. That suggests the TCP connection stayed open at the client layer but server/edge closed the upstream, or a middlebox swallowed the close. two quick asks: 1) what's the TLS/protocol (h2 vs http/1.1) used? 2) can they repro with curl on the same device and with --http1.1 and --http2 to compare?

luis-netops: my gut — carrier transparent proxy or mobile NAT gateway doing protocol rewrite/downgrade. some carriers downgrade http/2 streams to http/1.1 and mishandle chunked streaming. edge-proxy logs sometimes show a downgrade + immediate FIN if the downstream changes IP/port. ask customer to capture tcpdump if possible.

sam-eng: can we get relevant edge logs for req_0a1b2c? even just proxy hops and protocol negotiation lines. if it's a downgrade we should see a log like: 

```
edge-proxy[conn=XYZ] protocol_negotiation: client_h2 -> backend_http1.1; action=downgrade
edge-proxy[conn=XYZ] upstream_close: reason=half_closed_by_proxy
```

anya-support: pasted what we have from the customer (redacted): 
```
EDGE_LOG: conn=0x7f92ff proto=h2 -> backend=http/1.1, rewriter=transparent-proxy
EDGE_LOG: conn=0x7f92ff write_error: short_write, closing
HTTP: response_incomplete, client_seen_bytes=1234
```

kai-sdks: if a transparent proxy did a downgrade it can break SSE's chunked semantics. quick repro suggestion for customer: run locally on the device after connecting to WiFi, start stream, then run `sudo tc qdisc change dev <iface> root netem loss 15% && sudo ifdown <wifi> && ifup <wwan>` — but simpler: toggle airplane mode. also try curl with explicit `--http1.1` vs `--http2` and compare. e.g.: 

```
# http2 attempt
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=..."
# http1.1 attempt
curl --http1.1 -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=..."
```

sam-eng: also try increasing client keepalive/ping frequency to 10s. if middlebox is stateful and the TCP 4-tuple changes during NAT rebinding, a short ping might force a reconnect and avoid silent half-close. in mobile-js we have `client.setKeepAlive(10000)` (ms).

anya-support: customer asked if partial streams are billed — they saw partial JSON and were charged. billing team: are partial delivered tokens billable?

sam-eng: brief billing note (not legal): tokens generated by the model that were returned to the client are billable. partial vs complete response doesn't change that. billing@redwood can confirm if we need a credit.

luis-netops: actionables: 1) collect edge logs for that connection id/time range, 2) ask customer to run the two curl variants, 3) ask them to enable client keepalive at 10s and retry. if we can reproduce, we should add an edge flag `preserve_chunked_for_downgrade` to try to avoid closing on short writes.

kai-sdks: I'll draft a small diagnostic script they can run on device (non-root) to automate http2/http1 flip and capture client timing. will post here when ready. :hammer_and_wrench:

anya-support: told customer the workaround (enable keepalive, try http1.1 mode) and asked for tcpdump + curl outputs. escalated to eng if we can reproduce. customer appreciated quick triage. :white_check_mark:

sam-eng: moving to eng-runtime if we have reproduce steps + tcpdump. assigning follow-up to @sam-eng. closing for now from support side — will update thread with logs.

support-bot: ticket 12345 updated: status=escalated, assignee=sam-eng

sam-eng: noted. next steps: reproduce in lab with a small transparent proxy that rewrites ALPN -> force http1.1 and see if SSE half-chunk/close behavior occurs. will share results by EOD.
